A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same cognitive-distortion detection framework. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching retained appendix material across renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on KoACD and Therapist QA, including repeated-run F1 results, input ablations, and label-coverage analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and additionally reports direct prompt-based LLM classification results in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The proposed ELB extraction, three-LLM instance generation, MiniLM embeddings, multi-view gated attention, sentence-feature fusion, and classification loss remain unchanged. Additional rationale and revised experimental hyperparameters do not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same KoACD and Therapist QA classification tasks and populations. v2 clarifies primary-label selection for Therapist QA, consistent with the existing multiclass formulation; no new dataset, language, or test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Section 6.4 and new Appendix D add Gemini 2.0 Flash, GPT-4o, and Claude 3.7 Sonnet as directly evaluated classification baselines on both datasets. These models previously generated instances within the proposed pipeline. Their new comparator role substantially broadens the comparison beyond the retained MIL configurations and cited DoT result.

E3.justification: Tables 10–11 change the reported generation temperature from 0.7 to 1.0 and dropout from 0.5 to 0.3. The new direct-LLM comparison specifies matching ELB inputs and generation parameters. Existing splits, metrics, and learning-rate schedule remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The four ELB/salience configurations, missing-label analysis in Figure 4, per-type analysis in Table 7, and appendix instance examples and cross-dataset case discussion are retained. Shortening Section 7.1 and renumbering appendices do not remove the underlying analyses.

E5.justification: Section 6.4 retains ten randomized-split runs and mean ± standard deviation reporting, with unchanged uncertainty reporting in Tables 6–7. New Table 14 supplies baseline point estimates without introducing an additional run-count, seed, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: New Table 14 reports KoACD/Therapist QA F1 scores of 0.386/0.348 for Gemini, 0.325/0.332 for GPT-4o, and 0.272/0.318 for Claude, all below the reported MIL scores. This adds a supplementary comparison result set. Existing aggregate and per-type scores, instance statistics, and Figure 4 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 retain the same bag definition, salience normalization, attention operations, and feature fusion. Changing the salience symbol in the accompanying description is a notation correction. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain their substantive claims. Section 8 strengthens the application framing: v1 describes potential usefulness for early detection, whereas v2 explicitly claims that detection from single utterances before extended dialogue supports timely clinical intervention.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges the absence of formal human validation of intermediate ELB components and distortion instances, defines interpretability as attribution rather than validated clinical explanation, and adds proprietary-model portability limitations. It also interprets the new baselines as evidence that ELB prompting alone is insufficient and explains generation variability as intentional diversity.

D1.justification: v2 discloses primary-label selection for Therapist QA and a 100-epoch setting, documents baseline generation controls, and revises hyperparameter documentation. Frequency- and presence-penalty entries disappear. Learning-rate and embedding-dimension entries leave Table 11 but remain in the main text, so that information is retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 and the references add Qi et al. (2025), discussing standardized re-annotation and teacher-student multitask learning for generalization. The remaining related-work coverage and central MIL positioning are substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes tense and wording edits, rewrites the Therapist QA description, condenses Sections 7.1–7.2, and revises the conclusion and limitations. It inserts Appendix D and renumbers subsequent appendices while preserving the overall narrative and section organization.

P2.justification: v2 adds baseline Table 14, restructures hyperparameter Tables 10–11, and removes redundant total rows from Tables 8–9. Appendix material reflows, including a nearly empty PDF page 13. Figures 1–4 are identical, and the existing results tables retain their basic displays.

improvement.justification: The added direct-LLM comparisons strengthen the empirical context, while clearer label-processing details and explicit limits on intermediate-output validation and interpretability improve transparency. The gains remain limited: original scores persist despite revised reported hyperparameters without reconciliation, new baseline scores lack uncertainty estimates, and stronger clinical-use wording receives no new clinical validation. Overall, the added comparison and qualifications modestly improve the paper.
